introduction.value: Test suite for ChibiOS/VFS. The purpose of this suite is to verify the VFS infrastructure and drivers, starting with the path handling primitives used by the root driver.

description.value: The path normalization and absolute-path construction primitives are tested independently of a file system driver.
Absolute paths are normalized by removing redundant separators and resolving dot components.
The root path remains unchanged.

code.value: test_assert(vfs_test_path_normalizes("/", "/"), "root path normalization failed");

description.value: Repeated separators collapse to the root path.

code.value: test_assert(vfs_test_path_normalizes("////", "/"), "separator normalization failed");

description.value: Redundant separators and dot components are resolved.

code.value: test_assert(vfs_test_path_normalizes("/a//b/./c/../d/", "/a/b/d"), "component normalization failed");

description.value: Parent components cannot move above the root.

code.value: test_assert(vfs_test_path_normalizes("/../../a", "/a"), "root boundary normalization failed");

description.value: Only exact dot and dot-dot components are special; names beginning with dots are retained.
Dot-prefixed names are preserved.
A trailing dot component is removed.

code.value: test_assert(vfs_test_path_normalizes("/.", "/"), "dot component normalization failed");

description.value: A parent component at the root is removed.

code.value: test_assert(vfs_test_path_normalizes("/..", "/"), "root parent normalization failed");

description.value: Repeated parent traversal stops at the root.

code.value: test_assert(vfs_test_path_normalizes("/a/../..", "/"), "repeated parent normalization failed");

description.value: The source and destination may refer to the same buffer.
A path is normalized in its source buffer.
Relative paths are combined with a current directory, while absolute paths are normalized directly.
A relative parent path is resolved against the current directory.
Parent traversal stops at the root.
An absolute input ignores the current directory and is normalized.
Invalid relative inputs and insufficient output buffers are rejected, while an exactly sized buffer succeeds.
Path normalization rejects a relative input.

code.value: n = vfs_path_normalize(buf, "relative/path", sizeof buf); test_assert(n == (size_t)0, "relative path accepted");

description.value: Absolute-path construction rejects a relative current directory.

code.value: n = vfs_path_make_absolute(buf, "path", sizeof buf, "relative"); test_assert(n == (size_t)0, "relative current directory accepted");

description.value: An exactly sized output buffer succeeds.
A buffer without room for the terminator is rejected.

code.value: n = vfs_path_normalize(small, "/abc", sizeof small); test_assert(n == (size_t)0, "undersized buffer accepted");

description.value: A long normalized path exceeding the output buffer is rejected.

code.value: n = vfs_path_normalize(buf, "/123456789012345", sizeof buf); test_assert(n == (size_t)0, "long path overflow accepted");

description.value: A combined current directory and relative path that exceeds the output buffer is rejected.
Exact-fit and rejected paths must not write into the adjacent buffer.
Append terminates once and leaves the adjacent bytes untouched.
Reject overflow before writing outside the destination.
The absolute-path file system interface is tested using a minimal object derived directly from vfs_fs_c.
All file system operations dispatch through a vfs_fs_c object that has no process-aware driver interface.
Stat initializes the output and dispatches through the file system VMT.
Directory open dispatches through the file system VMT.
File open dispatches its path and flags through the file system VMT.
Unlink dispatches through the file system VMT.
Rename dispatches both paths through the file system VMT.
Directory creation dispatches its path and mode through the file system VMT.
Directory removal dispatches through the file system VMT.
The generic read-only open falls back from a file to a directory.
The generic writable open does not open a directory after the file system reports one.
Node information is initialized before dispatching through the node VMT.
Optional node information is cleared before the provider runs.
The overlay-derived root resolves relative paths and owns the current directory, plain overlays route absolute paths, and synthetic file systems report only metadata they own.

brief.value: Root path resolution and current directory.

description.value: Relative and absolute paths are normalized by the root, rename resolves both paths against one current directory, and failed directory changes preserve the path context.
A relative path is resolved against the root current directory before reaching the backing file system.
An absolute path ignores the current directory and is normalized by the root.
Both rename paths are resolved against the same current-directory snapshot.
Two roots sharing one file system keep independent current-directory contexts.
The current directory can be queried and an undersized destination is rejected.
A failed directory validation does not change the current directory.
A root with no backing file system validates and selects its synthetic root directory.
A plain overlay forwards borrowed absolute paths, exposes a synthetic root, and rejects relative paths without owning a current directory.
An absolute path is forwarded unchanged to the backing file system.
The overlay root has the same synthetic metadata when queried by path or through an opened node.
A relative path is rejected by a plain overlay.
The streams driver exposes consistent synthetic modes and sizes, selects one backend interface from each element mode, and routes terminal controls only to TTY nodes.
Path queries expose the synthetic directory and stream modes without optional metadata.
Opened nodes and directory entries report the same synthetic metadata as path queries, and unsupported control operations return ENOTTY.
FIFO and random-stream operations use the selected interface, while TTY controls are dispatched only to the terminal interface.

brief.value: Stream open capabilities and directory rejection.

description.value: Stream open capabilities and directory rejection.
Stream open capabilities and directory rejection.
HAL and XHAL share stable return-code values. TTY configuration failures become EINVAL while other failures retain the EIO fallback.
Shared status values preserve HAL compatibility and distinguish invalid state from an invalid instance.
Flush and flow configuration failures translate to EINVAL; successful operations still return success.
Unavailable drivers and other failures remain EIO, and non-terminal streams still reject TTY controls.
Unregistering or disposing an overlay leaves shared file systems alive until the caller disposes them.
Removing a mapping leaves the file system usable through another overlay and reports a missing mapping on subsequent unregister attempts.
Disposing overlays leaves registered and backing file systems intact, allowing their caller to dispose them exactly once after all overlays are gone.
The LittleFS driver reports its configured block size and obtains live sizes from opened file objects.
Path queries and opened nodes expose the configured block size, opened files report their live size, and unsupported metadata remains invalid.
Directory path and opened-node queries report the configured block size and no unsupported metadata.
An opened file reports its size before close, then its path reports the same size after close.

brief.value: Instance wrapper exclusion and independent progress.

description.value: A suspended LittleFS read blocks operations on its own instance while another filesystem can create and read files on an independent device.
Suspend one instance in storage I/O, queue a competing path operation, and use the other instance.
Check error exits, compound enumeration and per-instance lifecycle state.

POSIX open flag matrix.

description.value: The ROMFS driver reports allocation metadata only when the embedded representation makes it knowable.
Directories and dynamic files leave storage metadata unavailable, raw files expose payload blocks, and the built-in chunked backend also exposes its chunk size.
Directory path and opened-node queries leave optional metadata unavailable.
Raw files report their embedded payload allocation by path and through an opened node.
The built-in chunked representation reports its preferred chunk size and physical payload blocks.
Dynamic files update their logical size without claiming unavailable storage or timestamp metadata.
The FatFS driver reports cluster allocation and converts its timezone-less two-second timestamp into the VFS UTC representation.
Path queries expose cluster allocation and modification time, while opened nodes expose only metadata available from their live FatFS objects.
A closed file reports cluster size, allocated blocks, and its two-second modification timestamp.
An opened file reports live size and cluster allocation without claiming an unavailable timestamp.
Directory path metadata includes modification time, while an opened directory retains only cluster size.
Creation preserves existing contents unless truncation is requested, truncation without creation requires an existing file.
Creation without truncation preserves an existing file.
Truncation clears an existing file but does not create a missing file unless creation is also requested.
A suspended disk read keeps another node on the singleton filesystem out of native state; ordinary errors and directory iteration release the lock.
Hold a native read at disk I/O and attempt metadata access through another open node.
Exercise error exits and rewind/read without recursive mutex acquisition.
A failed immediate mount unregisters its native object before returning it to the pool.
POSIX open flag matrix.
POSIX open flag matrix.

description.value: Buffer pair reservation and pool waits.

brief.value: Buffer pair storage and pool capacity.

description.value: Both path slots alias one contiguous scratch view, and every pool element is aligned.
Reserve all configured pairs and check their layout and alignment.
An exhausted pool waits for a returned pair without holding an upper-layer lock.
Wait for a pair, then return the reserved pairs.
Root owns one pair per operation; overlays and ROMFS consume borrowed paths.
Backing routes receive the prefix through nested overlays; registered mounts bypass it.
Use only one pair and apply the prefix to backing path operations.
Rename retains both backing paths and bypasses the prefix on mounts.
Reject prefix overflow, accept an exact-fit path, and return the pair after errors.

brief.value: Nested overlays and ROMFS without scratch allocation.

description.value: Literal paths reach ROMFS without another allocation, and a root operation needs only one available pair.
ROMFS and overlays accept borrowed literal paths with the entire pool reserved.
One pair supports root file opens and a prefixed merged-root listing.
Combined opens and chdir retain logical paths with a single pair.
A second root operation changes CWD while the first retains its pair through open fallback, directory validation, or node cleanup.
Yield at each suspension point and let another thread change CWD before resuming.

brief.value: Live overlay enumeration and lazy CWD allocation.

description.value: Mount changes cannot restart backing iteration, and each root allocates CWD storage only when first needed.
Grow and shrink the mount table during backing iteration and after end of directory.
Queries and failed validation leave CWD unallocated; successful changes reuse one buffer per root.

brief.value: Matching metadata reader and writer protection.

description.value: Root CWD reads, overlay route lookup, and mount removal wait for the owning metadata mutex.
Hold metadata while a higher-priority worker attempts each operation, then release and verify completion.
A root waiting for a buffer pair leaves its metadata available to other operations.

brief.value: Root error cleanup across all path operations.

description.value: Normalization, prefix, missing-route and leaf errors return every pair and preserve CWD.
Reject overlong input and prefixes on every path entry, checking the pool after each return.
Propagate leaf and missing-route errors without retaining buffers or changing CWD.

brief.value: Sleeping routing owner and an exhausted pool.

description.value: A root caller waits for a pair while metadata remains accessible and the sleeping owner can finish.
Queue a root caller behind a sleeping owner, alternating successful and failed completion.
Resolve relative rename paths after the pool wait, using the CWD committed by the sleeping owner.

brief.value: Independent routing operations complete out of order.

description.value: Exercise every completion permutation with two or three pairs, including both rename slots and driver errors.
Resume sleeping operations in all orders and check their paths, results, and returned buffers.
File and typed directory scratch contend with root paths in both directions without an upper lock reaching callbacks.
Fill both scratch halves during a dynamic ROMFS read, then exercise directory scratch and an I/O error.

brief.value: Mount replacement during a paused route.

description.value: An in-flight call keeps its selected driver while later calls observe a replacement mount.
Replace a mount while its old driver sleeps, preserving the old driver until completion.

brief.value: Independent directory handles during mount changes.

description.value: Two open handles keep independent iteration positions while the mount table changes.
Interleave distinct iterators and update mounts after the first enters its backing phase.
Production newlib bindings retain nodes across close/reuse and release outside descriptor protection.

brief.value: I/O pins survive close and descriptor reuse.

description.value: Suspended reads and writes retain the original node through close/reuse, on success and error.
Suspended reads and writes retain the original node through close/reuse, on success and error.
A descriptor is reusable while disposal of its previous node is suspended.
A descriptor is reusable while disposal of its previous node is suspended.

code.value: test_assert(vfsIOInsert(&vfs_test_io, &vfs_test_io_nodes[0].node) == 0 && vfsIOGetDescriptorFlags(&vfs_test_io, 0) == 0, "installed reference has stale flags"); test_assert(vfsIOSetDescriptorFlags(&vfs_test_io, 0, VFD_CLOEXEC) == 0 && vfsIODup(&vfs_test_io, 0) == 1 && vfsIOGetDescriptorFlags(&vfs_test_io, 0) == VFD_CLOEXEC && vfsIOGetDescriptorFlags(&vfs_test_io, 1) == 0, "dup did not separate descriptor flags"); test_assert(vfsIODup2(&vfs_test_io, 0, 0) == 0 && vfsIOGetDescriptorFlags(&vfs_test_io, 0) == VFD_CLOEXEC, "same descriptor dup2 changed flags"); test_assert(vfsIOSetDescriptorFlags(&vfs_test_io, 1, VFD_CLOEXEC) == 0 && vfsIODup2(&vfs_test_io, -1, 1) == CH_RET_EBADF && vfsIOGetDescriptorFlags(&vfs_test_io, 1) == VFD_CLOEXEC && vfsIODup2(&vfs_test_io, 0, 1) == 1 && vfsIOGetDescriptorFlags(&vfs_test_io, 1) == 0, "dup2 flags or failure atomicity"); test_assert(vfsIOSetDescriptorFlags(&vfs_test_io, 0, -1) == CH_RET_EINVAL && vfsIOGetDescriptorFlags(&vfs_test_io, 0) == VFD_CLOEXEC && vfsIOGetDescriptorFlags(&vfs_test_io, -1) == CH_RET_EBADF && vfsIOSetDescriptorFlags(&vfs_test_io, 2, 0) == CH_RET_EBADF, "invalid descriptor flags accepted"); test_assert(vfsIOClose(&vfs_test_io, 0) == 0 && vfsIOGetDescriptorFlags(&vfs_test_io, 0) == CH_RET_EBADF && vfsIOInstall(&vfs_test_io, 0, &vfs_test_io_nodes[1].node) == 0 && vfsIOGetDescriptorFlags(&vfs_test_io, 0) == 0, "reused descriptor retained flags");

code.value: vfs_test_api_files[0].node.flags = VO_WRONLY | VO_APPEND; vfs_test_api_files[1].node.flags = VO_RDONLY; test_assert(vfsIOInsert(&vfs_test_api_io, (vfs_node_c *)&vfs_test_api_files[0]) == 0 && vfsIOInsert(&vfs_test_api_io, (vfs_node_c *)&vfs_test_api_files[1]) == 1 && vfsIODup(&vfs_test_api_io, 0) == 2, "access fixture failed"); test_assert(vfsIORead(&vfs_test_api_io, 0, &byte, 1) == CH_RET_EBADF && vfsIORead(&vfs_test_api_io, 2, NULL, 0) == CH_RET_EBADF && vfsIOWrite(&vfs_test_api_io, 1, &byte, 1) == CH_RET_EBADF && vfsIOWrite(&vfs_test_api_io, 1, NULL, 0) == CH_RET_EBADF, "descriptor access checks failed"); test_assert(vfsIOWrite(&vfs_test_api_io, 0, &byte, SIZE_MAX) == CH_RET_EINVAL && vfsIORead(&vfs_test_api_io, 1, &byte, SIZE_MAX) == CH_RET_EINVAL && vfs_test_api_files[0].calls == 0U && vfs_test_api_files[1].calls == 0U, "invalid I/O reached driver"); test_assert(vfsIORead(&vfs_test_api_io, 1, &byte, 1) == 1 && vfsIOWrite(&vfs_test_api_io, 2, &byte, 1) == 1, "stat permission bits confused with opened access"); test_assert(vfsIORead(&vfs_test_api_io, 1, shortbuf, sizeof shortbuf) == 1 && vfsIOWrite(&vfs_test_api_io, 2, shortbuf, sizeof shortbuf) == 1, "short driver transfer promoted to full count"); test_assert(__vfs_seek_target(INT32_MAX, VFS_SEEK_SET, 0, 0, &target) == 0 && target == INT32_MAX && __vfs_seek_target(1, VFS_SEEK_CUR, INT32_MAX, 0, &target) == CH_RET_EOVERFLOW && __vfs_seek_target(INT32_MIN, VFS_SEEK_END, 0, UINT32_MAX, &target) == 0 && target == INT32_MAX && __vfs_seek_target(0, VFS_SEEK_END, 0, UINT64_MAX, &target) == CH_RET_EOVERFLOW, "native offset arithmetic overflow");
